- `root>low` has `z-index: 1` and creates a stacking context (it's positioned absolutely)
- `root>low>inner` has `z-index: 999`, but it's confined within its parent's stacking context
- `root>high` has `z-index: 2` at the root level

Since `root>low` (z-index: 1) is below `root>high` (z-index: 2) in the root stacking context, all children of `root>low` — including `root>low>inner` regardless of its high z-index — are painted below `root>high`. The child's z-index only matters within its parent's stacking context, not globally.
